title: Conduct security control testing
summary: Control testing selects procedures that reveal whether an administrative, technical, or physical control is designed, implemented, and operating as intended.
outcome: Select and execute suitable control-test methods, preserve evidence, and interpret a result without confusing presence with effectiveness.
managerMindset: Test the control claim and its operating reality, not merely the existence of a policy or tool.

sections.title: Match method to control claim
sections.body: Methods include inquiry, observation, inspection, technical scanning, configuration review, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, code review, misuse-case testing, interface testing, synthetic transactions, and review of logs or samples. The method must fit the control and threat: a scan can identify exposure, while a controlled exploit tests exploitability and response but carries more risk.
keyPoints: No single method proves every control property.
Rules of engagement protect production and preserve evidence integrity.
Sampling and test coverage should be stated, not implied.

sections.title: Execute safely and preserve evidence
sections.body: Record the procedure, population, timestamps, tools, configurations, observations, exceptions, chain of custody where relevant, and tester identity. Protect sensitive findings and avoid changing the environment unnecessarily. Retest remediation using a procedure that can distinguish fixed, mitigated, accepted, and not-reproducible conditions.
keyPoints: Evidence must be sufficient, reliable, relevant, and traceable to the scope.
A finding's severity depends on context and likelihood, not only tool output.
Retesting is a separate evidence event.

workedExamples.title: MFA control test
workedExamples.situation: The organization claims all privileged access requires MFA.
workedExamples.reasoning: Sample privileged identities and authentication paths, inspect configuration, observe a controlled login, review exceptions and logs, and test service accounts separately. Document population and limitations; checking a dashboard screenshot alone is insufficient.

distinctions.difference: A vulnerability assessment identifies and prioritizes potential weaknesses; penetration testing attempts controlled exploitation to demonstrate impact and paths.

misconceptions.misconception: A clean automated scan proves the control works.
misconceptions.correction: Tools have coverage and configuration limits; validate the control's design, operation, exceptions, and relevant attack paths.

recallChecks.answer: The control claim, threat, environment, risk, safety constraints, and evidence needed.
Fixed, mitigated, accepted, unresolved, or not reproducible with supporting evidence.

scenarioSeeds.scenario: A code scanner reports no injection findings, but the test excludes generated SQL and production configuration.
scenarioSeeds.decision: Report the coverage limitation and test excluded paths with suitable methods.
scenarioSeeds.why: Tool output cannot support an unbounded conclusion.

studyPlan.learn: Review control-test methods and evidence handling.
studyPlan.connect: Connect testing to D7 logs/configuration and D8 secure-code testing.
studyPlan.apply: Design a layered MFA or backup-restore test.
studyPlan.revisit: Explain what each method cannot prove.

review.notes: Independent AI review only. Claim evidence, exact content fingerprints, scope checks, visual and memory-map assessments are recorded in knowledge/quality/. No human expert review or exam-readiness claim.

visualLearningContract.teachingQuestion: Which test safely produces evidence for the control/failure claim?
visualLearningContract.misconception: Penetration test is always the strongest or safest test.
visualLearningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
visualLearningContract.focalInsight: Select technique from claim, attack path, safety, scope, and evidence.
visualLearningContract.retrievalPrompt: Need prove API rejects unauthorized object access: which test/evidence?
visualLearningContract.textFallback:
control testing: test control objective. Decision: define expected behavior. Failure/example: deployment only
vulnerability testing: discover known weakness. Decision: validate exposure safely. Failure/example: scanner result treated exploit
penetration testing: authorized adversary simulation. Decision: set rules/stop conditions. Failure/example: unbounded production attack
code review: inspect implementation. Decision: trace security path. Failure/example: review misses runtime config
misuse case: abuse scenario test. Decision: derive negative path. Failure/example: happy path only
sampling: subset evidence. Decision: choose representative/valid sample. Failure/example: biased sample
